messages:
Anne: quick product question — for per-tenant span retention, should Console let customers pick an exporter (hot vs cold) directly or just set a TTL and let the gateway decide routing?
Raj: prefer TTL+gateway routing. keeps agents simple and avoids exploding agent config churn.
Maria: TTL in Console + gateway routing seems fine, but semantics need to be explicit: which traces get pinned to hot vs cold when TTL changes?
Kevin: concern: if we move a tenant from hot->cold, we must avoid slicing traces across stores mid-flight. trace completeness is priority.
Anne: proposal: gateway pins exporter at trace start using tenant effective config at ingest time. changes thereafter only affect new traces.
Raj: that avoids partial traces. side effect: gateway needs to persist trace->exporter mapping or compute deterministically. memory impact?
Maria: we can compute at start and annotate trace context with exporter id, then downstream routing reads the annotation. minimal state.
Kevin: still need to think about long-running spans and kv cache. Also tail-sampling/alerts: some tenants need retained traces for SLO investigations regardless of TTL.
Anne: UX feature idea: "incident retention override" — one-click on tenant page to bump retention to hot for N hours, auditable and RBAC gated.
Raj: model it as priority: tenant policy -> timed override -> global. overrides should be auto-expiring and create audit events.
Maria: gateway API sketch:
```yaml
GET /routing/tenant/{id}?version=42 -> {exporter: hot_s3, config_version: 42}
POST /routing/patch -> {changes, version}
```
Gateways accept a config version and refuse older configs.
Kevin: tests: config race e2e, verify trace completeness across config changes, billing reconciliation for hot/cold buckets.
Anne: agents stance? keep agents OTLP->gateway only. agents may send sampling hints but must not choose exporters.
Raj: agree. avoid per-tenant pipelines on agents. cardinality explosion if we try to create pipelines per tenant per-signal.
Maria: implementation detail: routing lookup cache with short TTL to bound memory on gateway. fallback to default exporter if cache miss and async refresh.
Kevin: metrics we need: traces_routed[tenant, exporter], bytes_routed[tenant, exporter], overrides_count, config_version_mismatch_rate.
Anne: Console UX: show "current exporter" badge on tenant overview, and a small timeline of recent retention changes with who triggered them.
Raj: security: only certain roles can hit override; wire changes into audit log + webhook export.
Maria: pitfall: config sync across gateway fleet. use versioned configs + graceful rollout. gateways reject traces older than last known config version to avoid silent drops.
Kevin: chaos tests: force config flip during high QPS, verify no partial traces and no silent drops. Also simulate override expiry.
Anne: next actions: I'll draft Console mockups and API surface for "tenant retention policy". @Maria please post a more detailed gateway lookup API and caching strategy. @Raj can you estimate cost delta if hot routing increases by 10%?
Maria: will post API sketch and a short perf note later today.
Raj: will run cost numbers, include egress + storage. ETA EOD.
ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: gateway-config-service v0.43 -> canary tomorrow 0400 UTC
Anne: thanks all — linking the UX PR and the retention epic to this thread in a bit.
